overview: This enum tells the computer opponent which evasive response to make against an incoming attack.

None.technical: FGameCharacterAction_AttackBase::GetAttackAvoidType returns this value when AttackRow is null, and the row constructor uses it as the default. UGameCharacterActionController::AttackActionUnknownSlot94 also returns 0 for an AttackDefault layer. The AI TypeA switch has no case for 0 and returns without pressing an evasion input.

Guard.simple: The computer opponent guards the attack.
Guard.technical: The attack row value reaches the AI through AttackActionUnknownSlot94. FGameCharacterAIAction_TypeA::Tick switches on AvoidType and calls PressGameKey with EGameInputKey::Guard for this value. A shikigami that should evade also sets AvoidType to this value before the switch.

DodgeStep.simple: The computer opponent steps toward an open side.
DodgeStep.technical: The AI feeds EGameInputKey::Guard into input data for AvoidType values 2 and 3. In the main switch this value calls SetStickToClearSide on phase 0 and StudioGameInputData88 with a zero FVector2D on the next phase, then toggles Phase between 0 and 1.

AwayStep.simple: The computer opponent steps away or to the side.
AwayStep.technical: The AI feeds EGameInputKey::Guard into input data for AvoidType values 2 and 3. In the main switch this value calls SetStickBackOrSide on phase 0 and StudioGameInputData88 with a zero FVector2D on the next phase, then toggles Phase between 0 and 1.

AwayDash.simple: The computer opponent dashes away from the attack.
AwayDash.technical: Values 4 and 5 call SetStickBackOrSide and enter the dash phase machine. This value presses EGameInputKey::Dash on phase 0 and again on later phases. It stops when the dash is not a normal dash and never presses EGameInputKey::Jump.

AwayDashJump.simple: The computer opponent dashes away and jumps.
AwayDashJump.technical: Values 4 and 5 call SetStickBackOrSide and enter the dash phase machine. This value presses EGameInputKey::Dash on phase 0, then presses Dash and Jump in later phases, including a combined Dash and Jump press on phase 4.

Invalid.simple: An invalid evasion request is ignored.
Invalid.technical: Declared as the 255 sentinel. FGameCharacterAIAction_TypeA::Tick has no case for it, so the avoidance switch reaches its default branch and returns without pressing an evasion input.

notes: The field name AttackAvoidType is reconstruction terminology and the action header marks its slot name as unproven. The numeric AI consumer paths are traced.
FGameCharacterAIAction_TypeA::Tick reads the value from the rival's slot-148 controller call when the rival's attack layer type passes its range test or when any attack timing is reached.
The read-only attack tables export Guard, DodgeStep, AwayStep, AwayDash, and AwayDashJump. None and Invalid are not exported.
